questionText:
Consider the following ANSI-C program.

The output of this program is ____________. (answer in integer)

Note: Assume that the program compiles and runs successfully.
explanation:
Step 1: Initial Variable Assignments
• $a = 5$
• $b = 11$
• $c = 20$

Step 2: Trace Pointer Operations
• ptr = &a; $\rightarrow$ ptr points to memory location of $a$.
• *ptr = c; $\rightarrow$ Dereferencing ptr assigns the value of $c$ ($20$) to $a$. Now, $a = 20$.
• ptr = &c; $\rightarrow$ ptr now points to memory location of $c$ ($c = 20$).

Step 3: Evaluate Remaining Statements
• a = *(&b); $\rightarrow$ Dereferencing the address of $b$ yields the value of $b$ ($11$). So, $a = 11$.
• c = *ptr - a; $\rightarrow$ Since ptr points to $c$, *ptr evaluates to $20$. Therefore, $c = 20 - 11 = 9$.

Step 4: Output
• printf("%d", c); outputs the value of $c$, which is 9.
